OWN-45.question: Ask CfA for the exact published address (or addresses) testers will open, for Streamlit's corsAllowedOrigins setting in run.sh.
OWN-45.why: Behind the IIS proxy, Streamlit refuses the browser's connection unless every published address is listed: the app looks started but the page never loads (confirmed live on 2026-09-17). Listing the address keeps the CORS and XSRF protections on.
OWN-45.background: The wrapper's run.sh carries a CHANGE-ME placeholder in --server.corsAllowedOrigins, one flag per address the browser shows. Its comment says the App Services team fills it in at deployment; the repo is ours on GHE, so confirm who edits it. Other fixed settings: the port comes from $PORT (8000; App Service recycles the container if nothing answers there), and the health check path is /_stcore/health. If the app is published under a sub-path, the app setting STREAMLIT_SERVER_BASE_URL_PATH must match it.
OWN-45.recommendation: Ask for the address and offer to commit the run.sh change yourself, so the repo and the deployed copy stay the same.
OWN-45.if_no_answer: The published page will not load, and the app cannot reach testers.
OWN-45.message_to_send: Published address: what exact address (or addresses) will testers open for our app? Streamlit needs each one in --server.corsAllowedOrigins in our run.sh, or it refuses the connection behind IIS and the page never loads. Will the app sit at the root or under a sub-path? And will your team fill that line in at deployment, or should I commit it to our repo?

OWN-46.question: Ask CfA to confirm IIS passes X-Windows-Auth-Header (DOMAIN\user) to pilot Streamlit apps and replaces any value a browser sends.
OWN-46.why: The header is how the app tells testers apart: their own folders, conversation lists, SharePoint folders and AI keys all hang on it. Without it everyone is one anonymous user sharing one conversation list and the shared key, which is unsafe for several testers.
OWN-46.background: The app reads the header from each request (its name can be changed with the WINDOWS_AUTH_HEADER setting) and trusts it without checking, because two controls outside our code make it safe: the App Service accepts traffic only from the IIS servers, and IIS overwrites any client-supplied value. If one request carries two copies of the header, the app trusts neither. Both DOMAIN\user and user@domain forms are understood; the form decides each tester's Key Vault secret name (OWN-43). Visible sign: each tester's sidebar shows 'Signed in as <their name>'. CfA's own starter code says the header is passed.
OWN-46.recommendation: Ask for written confirmation of both controls; privacy between testers depends on them. Then verify in the first-hour check: two testers, two names.
OWN-46.if_no_answer: Per-tester keys and folders do not work; all testers share one anonymous space and the shared key.
OWN-46.message_to_send: Identity header: please confirm that IIS passes X-Windows-Auth-Header with the signed-in DOMAIN\user to pilot Streamlit apps, overwrites any value a browser sends, and that our App Service accepts traffic only from the IIS servers. Is the value DOMAIN\user or user@domain? Our app relies on it to keep each tester's files, conversations and AI key separate.

OWN-47.if_no_answer: Assume Sol with images for everyone; the first-hour check's 'vision model' line confirms it.

OWN-48.question: Ask CfA whether the App Service runs in FIPS mode, as Funhouse and Foundry do.
OWN-48.why: Under FIPS one image-processing library (OpenCV) cannot load. The app already checks this safely and works around it, but the answer says whether free OCR of scanned pages could ever run there, which decides the OCR plan (VIS-11).
OWN-48.background: On a FIPS host OpenCV's bundled crypto library fails its self-test and kills the whole process, and every user's session with it. planlens therefore test-loads OpenCV in a separate process first and leaves raster work out if that test dies. Since 5.32.1 the find-every-copy tool (find_like) uses a numpy matcher and works without OpenCV, so the BACKLOG line saying it hides itself is out of date. Still lost under FIPS: the raster drawing reader and free OCR, so scanned pages with no text layer are read only by vision or by paid Azure Document Intelligence.
OWN-48.recommendation: A yes-or-no question for the list; plan as if the answer is yes.
OWN-48.if_no_answer: Assume FIPS: no OpenCV and so no free OCR there; the rest of the app is unaffected.
OWN-48.message_to_send: FIPS: does our App Service run with OpenSSL in FIPS mode, as other Department analytics platforms do? On those hosts one image library (OpenCV) cannot load. Our app already detects this safely and works around it; the answer tells us whether we can plan on free text recognition (OCR) for scanned pages there.

OWN-49.question: Ask CfA three leftover questions: does the Prompter gateway pass streaming; is a Nexus install acceptable, with which pins; what are the shared VM's limits?
OWN-49.why: Streaming keeps a long answer arriving instead of a silent wait. The install route and pins decide whether an update is a one-line pin bump. The VM limits decide whether heavy analyses (finite-element meshes, Monte Carlo runs) need throttling on a machine shared with other teams.
OWN-49.background: Streaming: the app streams by default; on dosdev, Connection diagnostics' 'streaming request' check tests it against the Prompter endpoint. If it fails, set the app setting GEOTECH_PROMPTER_DISABLE_STREAMING=1 (environment only; a .env line is ignored). Install: the wrapper repo holds only a few small files; the app arrives from Nexus as the released package, so an update is a pin bump plus an App Services sync. CfA fleet pins: streamlit 1.62.0, pandas 3.0.2, PyJWT[crypto] 2.13.0, msal 1.37.0, azure-identity 1.21.0, azure-keyvault-secrets 4.9.0; our test suites have not yet run on pandas 3 (TA-02). VM: multi-tenant, one slot; CfA monitors usage.
OWN-49.recommendation: Answer the streaming question yourself on dosdev first (Connection diagnostics) and drop it from the list if it passes. Ask the other two.
OWN-49.if_no_answer: Streaming stays on (switch it off if diagnostics fail), installs continue from Nexus, and heavy analyses run unthrottled on the shared VM.
OWN-49.message_to_send: Three smaller questions: (1) Does the Prompter gateway pass streaming responses, or should we switch streaming off? (2) Is it fine for our app to install as a released package from Nexus through packages.txt, rather than being copied into the repo, and which version pins do you expect beside your fleet pins? (3) What CPU, memory and run-time limits apply on the shared VM? A few of our engineering analyses are computation-heavy.

OWN-50.question: Ask CfA exactly what the Prompter returns when a key's monthly budget is spent: the HTTP status code and the response body.
OWN-50.why: The app is meant to tell a tester plainly 'your AI budget is used up' and stop retrying. That detection is built on guesses from other providers' replies. If the guess is wrong, a tester with a spent budget sees retries, a 'busy, try again' message or a raw error.
OWN-50.background: Today the app treats as a spent budget: status 402; error codes such as insufficient_quota or quota_exceeded; or phrases such as 'exceeded your current quota' or 'budget exceeded'. A 429 coded as a rate limit is treated as busy and retried up to four times, honouring any retry-after header. None of this has been seen live from the Prompter. Once CfA answers, a test pins the real reply (TA-06). Also useful: the day budgets reset, and what a rate-limit refusal looks like.
OWN-50.recommendation: Ask for a copied example response if they have one; a real sample is worth more than a description.
OWN-50.if_no_answer: Detection stays a guess; the first spent budget, read from a tester's activity log, becomes the sample.
OWN-50.message_to_send: Spent budget: when a key's monthly budget is used up, what exactly does the Prompter return: the HTTP status code and the response body (error code and message)? What does a rate-limit refusal look like, including any retry-after header? And on what day do budgets reset? We want testers to see a plain 'your budget is used up' message instead of an error or pointless retries.

OWN-51.question: Ask CfA to confirm that calling the Prompter directly with the pilot key is the sanctioned, metered route on Tiny Apps.
OWN-51.why: The Funhouse SDK's guidance says calling Azure AI directly, bypassing its metering, breaches the usage terms. On Tiny Apps the app calls the Prompter with a key, as CfA's own example code does. A written yes protects the pilot; a no would change how the app connects.

The app keeps its own per-turn record (activity.jsonl) but has no Funhouse meter on Tiny Apps.
OWN-51.recommendation: Ask; the expected answer is yes, and a one-line written confirmation is enough.
OWN-51.if_no_answer: The app keeps using the key route, which matches CfA's example code; the compliance question stays open in writing.
OWN-51.message_to_send: Metering: on Tiny Apps our app calls the Prompter endpoint directly with the pilot key, the same way your example code does, rather than through the Funhouse SDK, which cannot be installed there. Could you confirm this is the sanctioned route, and that usage is metered and logged on your side, so we meet the AI usage terms?

OWN-53.question: Ask CfA whether the app can reach the public, keyless USGS seismic design-maps service through Tiny Apps' API-First egress route.
OWN-53.why: That service returns ASCE 7 seismic design values for a site's coordinates, free and without licensing ASCE 7 itself (OWN-12). The App Service has no internet access, so outside services must go through API-First. The feature is not built; the answer decides whether it can be.

The idea was deferred until the pilot's networking answers. Today seismic site classes come from FEMA P-2082 and UFC 3-301-01 in the reference library.

OWN-53.if_no_answer: No coordinate-based ASCE 7 lookup; seismic values keep coming from the published references the library already holds.
OWN-53.message_to_send: Outbound access: the App Service has no internet access. Could our app call one public, keyless government web service, the USGS seismic design-maps service that returns ASCE 7 design values for a site's coordinates, through the API-First route? If so, how do we request it, and how long does approval usually take?

options.label: At the end of the Now train

OWN-57.question: The PyPI audit found the Department SharePoint site address and post names in published app releases. Accept, or delete releases once testers have moved on?
OWN-57.why: Your rule is no Department emails, hostnames or content in public places. PyPI files are public and cannot be edited, only deleted.
OWN-57.background: Audit 2026-10-13 of all 248 published files of your four PyPI projects (geotech-staff-engineer, planlens, geotech-references, geotech-report-extraction). No Department email appears anywhere; the only address is your Gmail as the author. App releases 5.10.0 to 5.33.0 (39 versions) carry the Department SharePoint tenant and team-site address in two webapp docstrings. App releases from 5.12.0 carry field-session post and project names in code comments, and report_ingest the embassy answer vocabulary (OWN-25). geotech-report-extraction (all 12 versions) describes an embassy report format and names a post in its test data. Funhouse, Prompter, SharePoint, CfA, Tiny Apps and Key Vault appear throughout the app as integration code, with no addresses. planlens and geotech-references are clean apart from naming Funhouse and Databricks as example hosts. Master already drops the SharePoint address (24b46df); the post names are INF-11.

options.label: Accept; keep the next release clean
options.effect: INF-11 scrubs master before the next release. Old files stay on PyPI; the SharePoint address needs a Department sign-in to use.

options.label: Delete the affected app releases after testers move on
options.effect: Permanent: those version numbers can never be reused, and any install pinned to one breaks. The Department's Nexus mirror and public PyPI mirrors keep their copies.

options.label: Also delete the geotech-report-extraction project
options.effect: Removes the older extraction package (superseded by report_ingest) and its post name from PyPI. Same mirror caveat.

OWN-57.recommendation: Accept the app releases and keep the next release clean (INF-11, including the 'the Department's ...' remarks). Delete the old geotech-report-extraction project: nothing of ours installs it (report_ingest replaced it), its GitHub repo is not public, and it is the one place that names a post and an embassy report format. Revisit deleting app releases with OWN-56 once testers are on the next release; deleting 5.33.0 now would break the dosdev install.
OWN-57.if_no_answer: INF-11 goes ahead before the next release; nothing on PyPI is deleted.
steps: Only if you choose to delete the old extraction project. Deletion is permanent and only you can do it.
Sign in at pypi.org and open 'Your projects'.
Next to geotech-report-extraction, choose Manage, then Settings.
Under 'Delete project', type the project name to confirm, then delete.
Record it on this card; Claude notes it in the backlog.
